doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Europe and a single mother's career
title: Why she never had an agent
summary: She was shy and afraid of leaving her daughter, got gigs through musicians' calls and Russell, and always found places to sing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Was there a reason why you didn‟t an agent? Did you not get offers or…?

I was shy, you know. And also, I was raising my daughter and I, I didn‟t want to be away from her for… You know, part of it was fear from being away from her and then part of it was I was shy, you know. I nev-- Nobody came knocking on my door… came to my door

knocking it down to, um, you know, to book me or to whatever, so… I, I think I got the Blue… uh, the Vanguard gig from George. I think George is the one that got me that gig, too. Then there was the Crazy Horse and different places. And Art D‟Lugoff‟s place. I always found a place to sing, you know, always, you know. But I started going to Europe a lot. And I still go to Europe a lot. And now I go to Japan at least, usually once a year. And um, I had started a workshop up at City College. Did I talk about that yet?
